summary.headline: APSEZ Q1 FY27 revenue and EBITDA each grew 19% YoY to INR 10,821 crore and INR 6,541 crore, with international ports EBITDA up 256%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 19% YoY to INR 10,821 crore and EBITDA rose 19% to INR 6,541 crore, despite Middle East disruption that hit trade from mid-February. Domestic ports revenue grew 12% and EBITDA 11% on only about 2% volume growth, driven by mix, fuel surcharge pass-through, premium container services and associated business services. International ports revenue hit a record INR 1,747 crore (up 80%) with cargo volumes nearly tripling to 22.8 MMT, helped by Australia and Colombo. Management declined to revise the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR 25,000-26,000 crore until after the first half. Management reiterated the Ambition 2031 targets and an 18-19% CAGR, and declined to comment on reported UK port acquisition talk.

financial_highlights.value: INR 853 crore, of which INR 518 crore is CT-3/CT-4 JV dividend
financial_highlights.change: Steady-state other income about INR 335 crore per CFO

segments.name: Domestic ports
segments.commentary: Revenue +12%, EBITDA +11%, EBITDA margin 74% on about 2% volume growth. Mundra grew 7%, with transshipment at 27% of volume vs a typical 23%. Krishnapatnam lost about 2-2.5 MMT due to a customer plant shutdown, which has now restarted.

segments.name: International ports
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,747 crore (+80%), EBITDA +256%, margin 41.8% vs 21.1%. Cargo volumes rose to 22.8 MMT from 7.7 MMT, driven by Australia and a strong Colombo ramp-up.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Trucking revenue +26% and international freight network revenue +28%. Rail volumes were down 19% in Q1 per the analyst's reference, with some stabilisation seen this quarter. FY26 logistics RoCE rose to 10%.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Revenue +67% to INR 901 crore with 135 vessels. Margin is below its mid-50s norm due to Middle East disruption; management's steady-state target is about 55%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR 25,000-26,000 crore is not being revised now; management will review after H1 FY27 results.
Management remains on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31 and targets 18-19% CAGR.
Capex guidance line was dropped from the presentation; the company will report the Q1 capex number with the Q2 balance sheet, and says it is slightly ahead of guidance.
Colombo Phase 2 is due to start in October 2026; Mundra's next container capacity addition is expected in calendar 2026.
Consolidated RoCE target: Ambition 2031 calls for about 1% incremental RoCE improvement per year to reach 20% by FY31; FY26 RoCE was 16%.
Marine steady-state margin target is about 55%; Australia port margin historically about 65%.
capex_capacity: Domestic port capacity is being expanded toward 1 billion MT under Ambition 2031, with major projects at Mundra, Dhamra, Vizhinjam, Ennore and Kattupalli, plus Hazira.
No new international port capex is planned in the next 5 years; focus is on utilising existing assets in Tanzania, Haifa, Australia and Colombo.
Mundra container capacity is close to full utilisation and the next addition is due in calendar 2026.
Colombo Phase 2 is due in October 2026.
Port-by-port capacity build-out is detailed on slide 23 of the Ambition 2031 deck.
demand_pricing: Domestic volumes were soft: Krishnapatnam fell on a customer plant outage, while Mundra recovered. Management says the East Coast share gain across Dhamra, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram and Gopalpur shows market-share gains.
Container volumes at Mundra in April and May were close to 700,000 TEU against a normal 740,000-750,000 TEU, with free storage of 45 days extended to the trade.
Realisations rose across liquid, container and dry cargo; container and liquid share of domestic cargo rose about 300 bps, lifting mix and realisation.
India trade grew only about 3% in the recent period versus a normal 6-8%. July showed improvement but is still not normal.
Vizhinjam and Colombo transshipment gains are structural (capacity-led and cost-led), not linked to the Middle East disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why are domestic volumes muted and what happened at Krishnapatnam and Logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a customer's imported-coal power plant outage at Krishnapatnam, which caused a 2-2.5 MMT shortfall; the plant has restarted. Mundra container volumes were hit by the Middle East disruption, and the Logistics ICD volumes weakened (Morbi near zero on LPG shortage, Tumb shifted to bulk).

qa_highlights.question: What drove domestic revenue growth well ahead of volume?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO and CEO cited fuel-surcharge pass-through, a richer cargo mix (liquid up more than dry; coal has lower realisation), premium emergency container services, and new associated business services. Management said cost was held nearly flat net of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state other income and JV contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Q1 other income of INR 853 crore includes INR 518 crore of CT-3/CT-4 JV dividends, so steady-state other income is about INR 335 crore. JV PAT ex-dividend was INR 230 crore vs INR 157 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given the strong Q1 EBITDA run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not revisit the INR 25,000-26,000 crore guidance now because of geopolitical and monsoon uncertainty. It will review after H1 FY27, once Q2 volumes are visible.

qa_highlights.question: What are the M&A criteria and leverage tolerance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management set four tests: a geopolitically and macro-stable country, a top-line and bottom-line contribution, local-currency financing, and returns at or above APSEZ average after adjusting for currency, inflation and cost of capital. It said leverage is 1.9x today and it would reach near zero in 5 years without M&A.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vizhinjam–MSC equity deal a template for international expansion, and what is the cash timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MSC equity partnership in Vizhinjam keeps Adani as operator, with no exclusivity, and partnerships are decided case by case. Cash flows are subject to regulatory and other approvals and will move only after they clear.

risks_watch: Middle East and geopolitical disruption: transshipment mix shift (Mundra 27% vs 23% typical) and recovery of Israel (Haifa) margins remain swing factors.
Trade growth: India trade is growing about 3% vs a normal 6-8%; July is improving but not normal. Monitor Q2 volumes before any guidance revision.
Pricing sustainability: the premium container and emergency charges and the 45-day free storage policy may not persist.
Krishnapatnam and East Coast volume recovery after the customer plant restart.
Logistics rail volume (reported as down 19% in Q1) and ICD utilisation (target 80% at four major ICDs not yet met).
M&A: a large international acquisition could dilute RoCE vs the 20% FY31 target; the reported UK port acquisition was not confirmed or denied.
Marine margin recovery to the about 55% norm; Vizhinjam regulatory approvals and MSC cash timing; Pipavav concession (2028) and Mundra concession discussions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and international performance, but cautious on the near-term outlook. Management was evasive on M&A rumours and on guidance revision, and repeatedly said Q2 and H1 will decide the FY27 view.
key_quotes: And this quarter has demonstrated that we can operate international businesses also with the same Adani DNA to bring the performance.
We remain firmly on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31.
So what we are focusing on are the three things.

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR 25,000-26,000 crore is held, not revised until after H1; Q1 revenue and EBITDA each grew 19%, with international ports up 80% and domestic volume only about 2%, and delivery rests on Colombo Phase 2 (October 2026), the next Mundra container addition (calendar 2026), and mix/realisation gains.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: International ports EBITDA margin rose to 41.8% from 21.1% and Marine margin is below its ~55% steady-state norm, which can recover; domestic margin is already 74% with fuel pass-through and mix gains, though the premium container charges may not persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (Colombo Phase 2 Oct 2026); Mundra calendar 2026
rows.why: Colombo Phase 2 is due October 2026 and Mundra's next container capacity addition is due in calendar 2026, with Mundra already close to full utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic volume grew only about 2% in Q1 and India trade is growing about 3% vs a normal 6-8%, but Krishnapatnam's 2-2.5 MMT shortfall has reversed after restart, international cargo nearly tripled to 22.8 MMT, and Colombo Phase 2 adds capacity in October 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Ambition 2031 build-out is under way at Mundra, Dhamra, Vizhinjam, Ennore, Kattupalli and Hazira and Q1 capex is slightly ahead of guidance, but no new international port capex is planned for 5 years and the Q1 capex number is only reported with Q2.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to revise the INR 25,000-26,000 crore FY27 EBITDA guidance despite a 19% Q1 EBITDA rise, citing geopolitical and monsoon uncertainty and India trade growth at about 3%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance is held, not cut, but India trade is about 3% vs a normal 6-8%, Mundra April-May volumes were near 700,000 TEU vs 740,000-750,000 normal, and the Middle East disruption persists.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or service launch was discussed beyond Colombo Phase 2 and the Mundra container addition, which are capacity adds rather than new products.

rows.label: Vizhinjam MSC equity partnership cash flows
rows.why: Cash flows from the MSC equity partnership in Vizhinjam move only after regulatory and other approvals clear, and no timing was given.

rows.label: Reported UK port acquisition
rows.why: Management declined to comment on the reported UK port talk, set four M&A tests, and noted leverage of 1.9x, which leaves room for a deal, though a large acquisition could dilute RoCE from 16% toward the 20% FY31 target.

rows.label: Marine margin recovery to ~55%
rows.why: Marine revenue rose 67% to INR 901 crore with 135 vessels, but margin is below its mid-50s norm due to Middle East disruption; recovery to the ~55% target depends on that disruption easing.
